newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian chancellor survives vote over bank deal.
newsitem.headline: Austrian chancellor survives vote over bank deal.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima on Thursday survived a no-confidence vote called by the far-right Freedom Party over privatisation plans for the country's top bank, Bank Austria.
Parliament voted against the no-confidence vote in the Social Democrat chancellor by 115 to 35.
It appeared opposition Greens and liberals had backed Klima, a former finance minister who took over as chancellor from Franz Vranitzky on January 28.

The vote was held after the nationalist far right condemned Klima for allegedly knowing that Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale had acquired first refusal on a majority stake in state-controlled Bank Austria.
"I was not informed," Klima told deputies before the vote was called. "This search for scapegoats is damaging to Austria's banks and economy," he added.
Far-right leader Joerg Haider answered in the debate by accusing Klima of being fully informed of the deal.
WestLB acquired a 10.7 percent voting stake in Bank Austria in 1995 and a first refusal on the majority stake held by Vienna City holding company AVZ.

The dominant Social Democrats stand accused of backing Bank Austria's acquisition of rival Creditanstalt in January in the knowledge that WestLB already had a first option on Vienna's 45.15 percent voting stake.

The Freedom Party said the Social Democrats had presented the Bank Austria-Creditanstalt deal as an "Austrian solution" to Creditanstalt's privatisation while knowing that the eventual sale of both to a foreign bank was on the cards.
